translations.title: You Were in the Water...
translations.text:
You were in the water

You were there, I saw you


All the cities

were weeping for you


The naked cities

bleating like beasts in a herd


At your passing

words were gestures

like these I offer you now


They thought they possessed you
because they knew how to type on your fan


But


No


You

were not there


You were in the water

where I saw you
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: They Are All There...
translations.text:
(Manual of Foams)


They are all there


Even those that kindle on fashionable nights


So much smoke rises from the sky
that it has rusted my eyes


The stars are sensitive to touch
I cannot type without them


They know everything

To temper the feverish sea
and cool my blood with their childish snow


Night has opened the piano
and I wave goodbye to them
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Hope
translations.text:
Who said the curve, the gold, desire are spent,
the rightful sound of moonlight on the marble,
and the perfect pleating of the wings
of cinema in its tender guardianship?


Search my pocket.
You will find feathers by virtue of birds,
crumbs searching for bread, moth-eaten gods,
words of eternal love without
a landing permit,
and the hidden path of waves.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Sitting on the Swing...
translations.text:
Sitting on the swing
the Angelus dozes


The stars and fruits fall silent


And wounded men
walk with their fountains
like lyrical dolphins


Others, more burdened,
with rivers on their shoulders,
pilgrim without knocking at the inns


Life is one endless verse


No one reached its end
No one knows heaven is a garden


Forgetfulness.


The Angelus has died


With bloodied scythe,
a reaper singing walked away.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: To C. A. Debussy
translations.text:
Sounds and perfumes, Claude Achilles,
turn in the air of the lovely night.
You know where a rose-note goes astray,
a rare fragrance of muted bugles,


subdued, of subtle castanets
and moonlight of guitars. Your lazy
orchestra, butterfly by butterfly,
opens ninety music stands to you.


Iberia, Andalusia, Spain in dreams,
slow Granadas, fragile Sevilles,
Giralda towers, three by eight, high Comares.


And metals in bloom, celestial woods
raise to cheek level
tears of carnations and orange blossoms.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Let Me Caress You Slowly...
translations.text:
Let me caress you slowly,
let me slowly make sure of you,
see that you are real, an extension
of yourself into yourself, without end.


Wave after wave shines from your brow
and gently, barely ruffling you,
your ten foams break as they kiss
your feet on the youthful shore.


Thus I love you, flowing and successive,
you, spring rising from yourself, furtive water,
music, languid to the touch.


Thus I love you, in small boundaries,
here and there, fragments, lily, rose,
and then your unity, light of my dreams.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: It Was in Numantia, as the Day Declined...
translations.text:
It was in Numantia, as there declined
the slow, august August afternoon,
Numantia of silence and ruin,
soul of freedom, throne of wind.


The light at moments became a mine
of transparency and fading,
diaphanous evening absence,
hope, hope of the portent.


Suddenly, where? A bird without lyre,
without branch, without stand, sings, raves,
floating atop its fever’s peak.


God’s living pulse dripped down to us,
God’s laughter and talk, free and bare.
And the bird, knowing it, sang.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: The Cypress of Silos
translations.text:
Upright fountain of shadow and dream
that grieves the sky with your spear.
Stream that almost reaches the stars,
wound around itself in mad endeavor.


Mast of solitude, island marvel,
arrow of faith, dart of hope.
Today, on the Arlanza’s banks, to you
my ownerless soul came, a chance pilgrim.


When I saw you solitary, sweet, steadfast,
what longing I felt to dissolve
and rise as you do, turned to crystal,


like you, black tower of arduous edges,
example of vertical deliriums,
mute cypress in Silos’ fervor.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Giralda
translations.text:
Giralda, pure prism of Seville,
leveled by plumb and star,
mold set in blue, unblemished tower,
palm of architecture without seed.


If the breeze makes your mirror shine before you,
do not behold yourself in it, Narcissus,
let not that maiden skin of yours change,
all orange beneath the sun that bows to you.


Against the lemon-tree moon,
your edge is the bevel, a barber’s blade
that refines its loveliest vertical.


Touch slips over its vain caress.
I want you Moorish, not Christian.
Nothing but volume: base and height.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Behold, Frozen, Crystalline...
translations.text:
Behold, frozen, crystalline,
on the virginal lap,
dead now to embrace,
those divine limbs.
The murderers fled.
What colorless solitude.
Oh, my Mother, do not weep.
How Mary wept.
Since that day they call her
the Virgin of Sorrows.


Who was the sculptor able
to give ivory its softness?
Who drove his chisel
through the naked marvel?
I, Mother, was the rough
artisan, I the profane one
who shaped with my own hand
that triumph of death
over which your pity pours
warm pearls in vain.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Before the Towers of Compostela
translations.text:
Stone, too, takes flight when stars are out.
Over the cold, beveled night,
grow, twin lilies of daring;
grow, surge, towers of Compostela.


Your brow longs for a field of stars,
silent mistresses of persistence.
In my breast—oh, love—my fantasy
builds higher towers. The soul keeps vigil.


And she—you—here with me, though your fingers
cannot reach my towers of hope
as mine can touch these stone ones,


look through my towers at the stars,
not these of autumn—erase them; those
of our August burning in cold dreams.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Sleeplessness
translations.text:
You and your naked sleep. You do not know.
You sleep. No. You do not know. I lie awake,
while you, innocent, sleep beneath the sky.
You for your dream, ships for the sea.


In prisons of space, airy keys
lock you away from me, confine and steal you. Ice,
glass of air in a thousand sheets. No flight
can lift my birds’ wings to you.


To know you sleep, certain, secure—
faithful channel of surrender, pure line—
so near my shackled arms.


What dreadful islander’s captivity:
I, sleepless, mad, on the cliffs,
ships on the sea, you in your sleep.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: The Walnut Tree’s Shadow
translations.text:
The walnut tree’s shadow is dangerous

Dense in October like a vault,
like an unmoving dome,
it shelters us and invites us
to its cool caress
and fruits fall one by one,
tortured brains, walnuts, walnuts


At night
shadow of dead moon from the walnut tree
and its plaintive leaves
kill themselves one by one
and unknown, invisible feet
tread them down, crush and bury them,
thus freeing them
from the windy whirlwind
that lashes what is mortal, abandoned
on the earth’s grim surface,
impenetrable


But who passes, who pauses?
Whose are those merciful, redeeming feet?
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Picture
translations.text:
The sky’s torn tablecloth
is my standard
and the liquor of sunset
reflects on art


I prefer the enclosed sea
and I put a mute on the sun
My poetry and apples
make the atmosphere finer


In the middle, the guitar
Let us love her


She gathers the surrounding air
She is the new nakedness,
Venus of the century, or Madonna without child


Beneath her strings rivers flow
and birds drink water without staining it


After seeing the picture
the moon is more precise
and life more beautiful


The household mirror tries on a smile
and in a transport of passion
water sings, caged in the bottle.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: The Three Sisters Were There...
translations.text:
(The Bride’s Ballad Book)


The three sisters were there,
the three from every tale,
the three up on the balcony
weaving lace and dreams.


I walked down the street
and looked up… My dry footsteps
echoed, forgotten,
in the evening silence.


The eldest looked, curious,
and the middle one, laughing,
looked at me and said something to you…
You embroidered in silence


as though you did not care,
as though it frightened you.
Then you stood up
and told me a secret

in one long gaze,
long, long… The reflections
in the blurred windowpanes
erased the outline of your slender


profile. Your figure was
the flower in a halo of dream.
…Three you were, three sisters,
as in the storybooks.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Child Days Sing at My Window...
translations.text:
Child days sing at my window


All the houses are made of paper
and the swallows come and go,
folding and unfolding corners


Violators of roses,
eternal enjoyers of things’ ivory,
here is the nest built for you
on the hardest crane


And from it you will all sing
in the hands of the wind


My life is a lemon
but my song is not yellow


Lemons and planets
in the sun’s branches
how often you sheltered
the green shadow of my love
the green shadow of my love


Spring is born
and rain grazes in its body of light


The rainbow springs from prison


And over the rooftops
my white hand is a hotel
for doves of my faithless sky
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: To Drag the Fainting’s Tail for a Long Time...
translations.text:
To drag the fainting’s tail for a long time
without fearing fragrance might rebel
Let oneself flower through the month of May
with wallflowers: hands, eyes of distance


Forgive the rain its deep vocation,
its love of statues, its noble shaping;
forgive it, though later we know the schoolyard garden
floods with mutilated torsos


Forget the perfumes that make colors weep
deserve the foreshortenings that renew the air
resign, abdicate crowns and splendors,
fabulous ties lost carelessly


Because, dear friend, all is balanced now: 
my debts, your jasmines, celestial disorders,
the dead man stretching, the snail that thinks,
and the turtledove’s wing extending hospitals.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: When He Comes, Oh, I Do Not Know...
translations.text:
When he comes, oh, I do not know
what I will wrap him in,
what.


Oh, tell me, moon,
when in your arms of enchantment
you take the sturdy oak
and rock him in your cradle.
Tell me, I do not know
what I will touch him with,
what.


Oh, tell me, breeze,
who with your kisses so light
stir the highest leaf,
comb the smoothest feather.
Tell me, and I will not say
what I will kiss him with,
what.


And now, as I remember,
Angel of the Lord, you,
tell me, for I received
your message: “behold the handmaid.”
Yes, tell me, by your faith,
what I will embrace him with,
what.


Or tell me, if not you,
if you know, Joseph,
and I will obey you,
for I am only a girl;
with what hands shall I hold him
so he will not break, oh,
with what.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Song
translations.text:
(Until Always)


Words are made from autumn shadow,
from words, clouds, clouds,
from clouds, cheeks,
from your cheeks the sun is born on even days,
the cold moon on odd ones,
did you know it, perhaps?


With sun and moon
the cymbals touch
and my trees dance.
Your two eyes come to the dance,
your eyes, navigable with the breeze.
From the breeze come
the most secret favors,
and the world, since it exists,
will turn to ash,
did you know it, perhaps?


Ash that seeks a nest in your fingers,
smoke falling in love with your lips,
fire drawing near your side,
look in the sky: clouds, your cheeks, ours,
my autumn words that make
the leaves,
the leaves of your feet,
did you know it, perhaps?
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Ballad of the Duero
translations.text:
River Duero, river Duero,
no one comes down to keep you company;
no one stops to hear
your eternal stanza of water.


Indifferent or afraid,
the city turns its back.
It will not see in your mirror
its toothless wall.


You, old Duero, smile
among your silver beards,
grinding with your ballads
the poor harvests.


And among stone saints
and magical poplars
you pass, carrying in your waves
words of love, words.


Who could, like you,
both still and moving,
always sing the same verse
but with different water?


River Duero, river Duero,
no one comes down to be with you,
no one wants to heed
your eternal, forgotten stanza,


but lovers,
who ask about their souls
and sow in your foam
words of love, words.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Verses
translations.text:
(Escape)


Verses, verses, more verses,
verses
for good men, sublime in their ideals,
and for the wicked;
verses
for Philistines, clumsy and incorrigible,
and poets of smooth lakes.

Verses
on the fronts
and backs
of loose and scattered papers.

Verses
for the faithless, for apostates,
for converts,
for just men
and the inverted;
verses, verses, more verses,
poets, always verses.

Let us drown the positivists in verses,
leave them submerged
beneath the enormous wave of verses,
sunken in it, shipwrecked, immersed.

Verses
in holy daily labor
and in fugitive, crosswise moments.

Traditional verses
and new, strange, varied verses.

Verses,
verses,
more verses,
verses,
verses,
And verses,
always verses.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Not Seeing You
translations.text:
One day and another day and another day.
Not seeing you.


I could see you, know you walk so near,
that fortune’s miracle is possible.
Not seeing you.


And heart and reason and compass,
all three fail. No one can find you.
Not seeing you.


Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, not finding you,
not breathing, not being, not deserving you.
Not seeing you.


Desperately loving, loving you,
and being born again to love you.
Not seeing you.


Yes, born anew each day. All is new.
You are new, my life, you, my death.
Not seeing you.


Groping (though it was midday)
in infinite fear of breaking you.
Not seeing you.


Hearing your voice, smelling your scent, dreams,
ay, mirages the desert reverses.
Not seeing you.


Thinking that you flee me, desire me,
would wish to find yourself in me, lose yourself.
Not seeing you.


Two ships at sea, their sails blind.
Will their wakes kiss tomorrow?
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Green Water, Green, Green...
translations.text:
Green water, green, green,
enchanted water of the Júcar,
green from the mountain pinewood
that almost saw you in your cradle


—woods of Saint Sebastians
in the dark sierra,
whose wounded sides
weep golden resin—;


green of green bodices,
green eyes, green moons,
of the beehives, palaces
lesser realms of sweetness,


and green—the early blush
that rises in your foam—
of dreaming, dreaming, so young,
of Mediterranean weddings.


Poplars, so many poplars
kill themselves for your sake,
breaking green glass
of your green, green urn.


Cuenca, all silver,
wants to see herself naked in you,
and stretches on tiptoe
over her thirty columns.


Do not think so much of weddings,
do not think, water of the Júcar,
that you grow so green you turn indigo,
purple, and blue.


Do not paint yourself so soon
in colors that are not yours.
Your lips will taste of salt,
your breasts will taste of sugar


when, so green, green,
where will bodices and moons be,
pines, poplars, and towers,
and dreams of the high Júcar?
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Farewell to Pedro Salinas
translations.text:
The sky grows calm
Salinas when it sounds


Verbs sing on vacation,
prayers and conjugations


I will be, you will be, he will be
Yesterday’s image will return tomorrow


The image doubles the omen
Do you pray when thunder rolls the trisagion?


The world is poisoned
Salinas when it sounds no more


The most exquisite music
is the silence of the beloved mouth


To love, to love, and always to love
to have loved, to be destined to love


And from grandmother’s stocking
ounces fall smelling of cinnamon


The sky reddens
Salinas when it rocks you


Blushing was your kingdom
So much beauty all around


Rose and blue, blue and rose
Careful, do not let it break


And through your eyes, the squall
and the gale and fear of fairies


The sky turns olive-green
Salinas when it cradles you


Have you seen the olive tree in bloom?
Yes no yes no, subjunctive chance


Have you ever seen the stag’s autumn,
have you not learned to shed a verb’s leaves?


December comes and the oak weeps
and the coconut palm of Poor Port


The world is frightened
Salinas when he sings no more


Verbs sing in school
The sky is round, sails full


Pedro Salinas Serrano? Missing
And suddenly the children fall silent


They seek refuge in one another
Everything clearer, much clearer


The sky wants to love me
Salinas when he puts you to sleep
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: To My Friends in Santander Who Celebrated...
translations.text:
To my friends in Santander who celebrated
my professional appointment.


I ought now to say, “Friends,
thank you,” and sit down, without filler rhymes.
Allow me to say it in a lyrical tone,
in verse, yes, but free and fanciful.
Friends:
in a few days I will find myself surrounded by boys,
clumsy boys and clever ones,
gentle and prickly,
many leagues from my Santander,
in an ancient town,
quiet
and cold,
and I will speak to them of verse and half-lines,
and Dante, and Shakespeare, and Moratín the son,
and pluperfects and participles,
and one will yawn and another wink at me.
And another, surely the cleverest,
will give me a final nickname.
And so monotonous, lengthy school years will pass.
But one day I will have a pupil,
a true pupil,
and shape his child’s soul
and make him become new and different,
different from me and everyone: himself.
And he will keep respect and affection for me.
And now I say to you:
Friends,
let us drink to that boy,
to that chosen pupil,
that my stiff fingers
may shape his spirit well,
and my lyrical flame catch in his virgin heart,
and that he may follow his way
whole and clear,
and because this pupil of mine,
who will immortalize my name and surname,
…may be the son,
the son
of one of you, my friends.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Lilies in Their Shirts
translations.text:
Come hear the roses and lilies
with their slender, unruly laughter
Come see the roses without chains
the lilies in their shirts


Come, instinct’s Amazons,
knights without spurs,
here to the garden grafted into a maze
of sunflowers and connecting rods


Music held up by nickel
urgently combs curved hair
and there is only one flushed cheek
and a golden oriole that lies


Sour the flavor of this feverish minute
all spattered with favors
when a nightingale of nightingales
recommends mourning to the jasmine


When the one returning from whistling alone
the waltz “No More, I’m Dying”
begins to chase through corollas
the certainty of a hat


No, my friends. Let harmony return
and the carnations’ well-being
My heart, friends, was once
a tender gallop of horses


I want to live. Life is a new style
a spout of love, a spout of tears
Giraffe of living, your neck held high,
I spur you on and lift you


Pass, light riders of dawn,
toward a violet west
Far from me the treacherous trumpet
and your canters at a slowing pace


The clouds keep sharpening their edges,
more decisive each day
At their touch may the elective nerves
fill with chords


My hands brush sharp gifts,
warm and happy moons
Know that from today the lilies
and roses walk naked
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Albert Samain Would Say, Vallejo Says...
translations.text:
Albert Samain would say, Vallejo says,
Gerardo Diego, struck dumb, will say tomorrow,
once and only once: Stone of astonishment
and sweet wood of the stable, dear friend,
brother in the twin pursuit of hats
shaken loose by the speed of the stars


Stone of astonishment and noble stable wood
make up your daring raw material,
before the pendulum’s decrees and the
centuries-old creation of swallows.
You were born in a cemetery of words,
a night when the skeletons of all intransitive verbs
proclaimed a strike against “I love you forever ever ever,”
a night when the moon wept and laughed and wept
and laughed again and wept,
tossing itself for heads or tails.
And heads came up, and you lived among us


Since that night many barely born words died suddenly,
such as Caress Perhaps Category Brother-in-law Cataclysm
And others never heard before were lit upon the earth,
such as Mother Look Dying Melchizedek Miracle
and all those ending in an innocent tail


Vallejo, you live surrounded by birds on all fours
in a world that is dead, stone dead and rotten.
You live with your dead and living words.
And thanks to your being alive, we, the written-off, manage to lift our eyelids
to see the world, your world, with the mule and
the man guillermo-secondary and the tenderest girl and
the knives that hurt the palate
Because the world exists and you exist and we will probably
come to exist too
if you insist and sing and call out
in your brave valley, Vallejo
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Anyone Can Say “I Loved”...
translations.text:
Anyone can say “I loved.”
This desolating truth:—
Everything in the world is illusion,
there is no true happiness
nor constant feeling.
“I loved” means: nothing
ever suffices for man;
the most delicate passion,
the most sacred promise,
are smoke and wind… and nothing more!
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Epitaph
translations.text:
To be engraved on the grave of a skeptic


Imitation of Parny





He who lies here was supremely wise:
to avoid error, he doubted everything.
He called God’s existence into question,
and—doubting life—lived in his own way.

At last, tired of such profound chaos,
he hurried through this door,
to go and ask in the other world
what a prudent man should believe in this one.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: To the Moon
translations.text:
Sun of the one who keeps sad watch!
Star of cold radiance,
whose trembling rays shine only
to show the shadows of night!


Oh, how you resemble
the pale memory of past joy,
which makes the soul see nothing
but shadowy solitude!


Reflection of a flame
now hidden or extinguished,
you fill the mind, but do not kindle it;
you live in the soul, but do not animate it.


You reveal, like yourself, the shadows
you enamel and caress;
and only mute pain beholds you,
keeping fervent vigil.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: The Unwelcome Memory
translations.text:
Will you be the eternal companion of the soul,
tenacious memory of swift delight?
Why does endless recollection endure
if joy passed like a fleeting breath?


You, black oblivion, whose fierce hunger
opens your dark mouth without cease,
vast tomb of a thousand glories
and last consolation of pain!


If none is amazed by your vast power
and you rule the world with your cold scepter,
come! My heart names you its god.


Come and devour this impious phantom,
pale shadow of pleasure past,
dark cloud of pleasure yet to come.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: My Malady
translations.text:
In vain your friendship anxiously tries
to guess the ill that torments me;
in vain, my friend, moved, my voice attempts
to reveal it to your tenderness.


The longing, the madness can be explained
with which love feeds its fires;
pain, the most violent rage,
can breathe its bitterness through the lips.


But to speak of my deep unease
my voice and thought can find no means,
and when I search its source I lose myself:


yet it is a terrible, incurable ill,
that makes life hateful, the world hateful,
that dries the heart… In short, it is tedium!
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Love’s Torment
translations.text:
Happy is the one who sighs beside you, for you,
who hears the echo of your ringing voice,
who adores the charm of your laughter
and breathes the soft fragrance of your breath!


Such fortune, which the cherub in heaven
admires with envy,
troubles the soul, devours the heart,
and dies upon the clumsy tongue as it is told.


The world disappears before my eyes
and through my veins I feel coursing lightly
the fire of profound love.


Trembling, in vain I try to resist you.
I flood my cheek with ardent tears.
Delirium, joy, I bless you and die!
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Desire for Vengeance
translations.text:
O mighty spirit of the hurricane,
rugged as the grief that stirs me!
Come, excite my fury with your own!
Come, inflame my mind with your breath!


Let lightning buzz and burst with a crash,
while—like a dry leaf or withered flower—
your mighty blast hurls the oak
broken and shattered into the roaring torrent!


From the soul that calls and follows you,
envious of your destructive strength,
cast forth confusion in its turn.


Come… let your powerful wrath
take the place of the pain that madly devours her,
and dry the tears she weeps in cowardice!
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Imitating an Ode by Sappho
translations.text:
Happy is the one who sighs beside you, for you!
Who hears the echo of your ringing voice!
Who adores the charm of your laughter
and breathes the soft fragrance of your breath!


Such fortune—which the cherub in heaven
admires with envy—
troubles the soul, devours the heart,
and dies upon the clumsy tongue as it is told.


The world disappears before my eyes,
and through my veins I feel coursing lightly
the fire of profound love.


Trembling, in vain I try to resist you…
I flood my cheek with ardent tears,
I rave, rejoice, bless you, and die!
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: To the Stars
translations.text:
Silence reigns: meanwhile, bright
lights of peace, pure stars,
beautiful lamps of the happy night,
you embroider its funereal cloak with gold.


Pleasure sleeps, but my grief keeps watch,
and my laments break the silence;
the echo answers, in unison with them,
the sinister song of nocturnal birds.


Stars, whose modest, pure light
the sea’s blue mirror doubles!
If the bitterness moves you to pity


of the intense grief I lament,
how can you offer not even a pale reflection
to brighten my dark night?
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: O Mighty Spirit of the Hurricane...
translations.text:
O mighty spirit of the hurricane,
who today leave the forbidden region free,
come, excite my fury with your own!
Come with your fire to crown my brow!


Let lightning burst with a crash,
while like a dry leaf or withered flower
your mighty blast hurls the oak,
broken and shattered into the roaring torrent.


Come free me from the strange grief
that devours a proud soul with shame
and dims reason’s pure brightness.


Come! Give your power and furious wrath
to the inert heart that implores you,
and dry the tears it weeps in cowardice.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: In Vain Your Friendship Anxiously Tries...
translations.text:
In vain your friendship anxiously tries
to guess the ill that torments me;
in vain, my friend, moved, my voice attempts
to reveal it to your tenderness.


The longing, the madness can be explained
with which love feeds its fires…
Pain, the most violent rage,
can breathe its bitterness through the lips.


But to speak of my deep unease,
my voice and thought can find no means,
and when I search its source I lose myself:


yet it is a terrible, incurable ill,
that makes life hateful, the world hateful,
that dries the heart… In short, it is tedium!
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Pearl of the Sea! Star of the West!...
translations.text:
Pearl of the sea! Star of the West!
Beautiful Cuba! Your brilliant sky
night covers with its opaque veil,
as grief covers my sad brow.


I am leaving!… The busy crew,
to tear me from my native soil,
hoists the sails, and, ready to assist,
the breeze comes from your ardent zone.


Farewell, happy homeland, beloved Eden!
Wherever fate in its fury drives me,
your sweet name will delight my ear!


Farewell!… The swelling sail creaks…
the anchor rises… the trembling ship
cuts through the waves and flies in silence.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: To God
translations.text:
Is it not madness, Lord? You, absolute
in beauty, power, intelligence;
You, whose essence is perfection
and whose sacred attribute is happiness;


You, to me—who am born and die like a beast—
You, to me—who inherit evil—
You, to me—a frail being whose impotence
bears only sterile pain as fruit…


You seek me, O God! You accept my love
as a victory won
by your love over my free will?


Yes, it is no madness: for lowly dust
it is worthy of your supreme power
to make capable of adding to your glory!
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.
